_about: Muscle pull (Phase 6d). Force of a muscle = its PCSA (all muscles equally active, as in spasm after a fracture). It acts at each attachment (model/<region>/muscles.json, from Z-Anatomy) along the muscle's own path. Forces on the fragments give the DIRECTION of the typical displacement; the SIZE is a teaching value (below). The leg (tibia, fibula, patella) moves with the femur fragment that carries the knee; the fragment that carries the femoral head turns in the acetabulum but does not move out of it. Not modelled: gravity, ligaments and capsule (except the patellar ligament, which holds the distal patella), wrapping of a muscle round bone further than its attachment, the bed.

sizes._basis: Teaching values chosen by the engine author; no published source for the sizes.
sizes._leg: The leg-carrying fragment: each part of its turn takes its direction from the muscles and a teaching size: roll about the long axis 15 deg, sideways 5 deg, forwards/backwards 10 deg but only if the fracture is within 120 mm of the knee (the leg lies on the bed; a long lever cannot swing). The tibia and fibula follow it, except for the forwards/backwards tilt, which the knee joint takes up.
sizes._turn: Other fragments: axis of the turn from the muscles, size = the teaching value, used when the turning effect is at least 2 % of (total force x 30 mm).

end_share._about: Share of a muscle's force carried by each bone it is fixed to (default: all of it at every end).

Gluteus maximus muscle.r._basis: Most of gluteus maximus inserts into the iliotibial tract and only its deep lower part into the gluteal tuberosity (Gray's Anatomy). 25 / 75 is the author's split; no published ratio found.
